overview: This Senate resolution designates February 2026 as "American Heart Month." It describes cardiovascular disease, which includes heart disease and stroke, as the leading cause of death in the United States and lists major risk factors such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol, smoking, poor diet, lack of exercise and diabetes. The resolution supports raising awareness, research and access to affordable care, recognizes efforts to address the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on heart health, and encourages everyone to learn their own risk. The Senate approved it on February 25, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution helps spread awareness about the nation's leading cause of death and encourages people to learn about steps that can lower their risk.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for heart disease research or care.
